title: SQL Server Aliases
description: Learn how to use column aliases and table aliases in SQL Server to make your queries more readable and meaningful.

data.text: In this tutorial, you will learn how to use SQL Server aliases, including column aliases and table aliases, to make your queries more readable and meaningful.
When you use the SELECT statement to query data from a table, SQL Server uses the column names as the column headings for the output. For example:

data.title: Default Column Headings
data.content: SQL Server uses the column names as headings.
data.code:
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name;

data.text: To obtain the full names of customers, you can concatenate the first name, space, and the last name using the concatenation + operator. However, SQL Server returns the full name column as (No column name) which is not meaningful.
To assign a column or an expression a temporary name during the query execution, you use a column alias.

data.title: Column Alias Syntax
data.content: Use AS keyword to assign a column alias. AS is optional.
data.code:
column_name | expression AS column_alias

-- Without AS keyword:
column_name | expression column_alias

data.title: Using Column Alias
data.content: Assign a meaningful name to a concatenated expression.
data.code:
SELECT
    first_name + ' ' + last_name AS full_name
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name;

data.text: Note that if the column alias contains spaces, you need to enclose it in quotation marks:

data.title: Column Alias with Spaces
data.content: Enclose aliases with spaces in quotation marks.
data.code:
SELECT
    first_name + ' ' + last_name AS 'Full Name'
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name;

data.text: When you assign a column an alias, you can use either the column name or the column alias in the ORDER BY clause because SQL Server processes the ORDER BY clause after the SELECT clause.
A table can be given an alias, which is known as a correlation name or range variable. Similar to the column alias, you can assign a table a temporary name with or without the AS keyword:

data.title: Table Alias Syntax
data.content: Assign a temporary name to a table.
data.code:
table_name AS table_alias
-- or
table_name table_alias

data.text: For example, when joining multiple tables, table aliases improve readability significantly:

data.title: Using Table Aliases in a JOIN
data.content: Use table aliases to simplify column references in joins.
data.code:
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    order_id
FROM
    sales.customers c
INNER JOIN sales.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

data.text: In this query, c is the alias for the sales.customers table and o is the alias for the sales.orders table. When you assign an alias to a table, you must use the alias to refer to the table column. Otherwise, SQL Server will issue an error.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Use table aliases when joining multiple tables or when referencing the same table more than once in a query. They make queries shorter and easier to read.

items: A column alias is a temporary name assigned to a column or an expression in a query's result set.
Use a column alias to rename the output of a column or an expression to make it more meaningful.
A table alias is a shorthand or temporary name assigned to a table in a query.
Use table aliases when joining multiple tables or when referencing the same table more than once in a query.
